name: BEBC
summary: BEBC was a large CERN bubble chamber used with several target fills and neutrino beams. It supported multiple collaborations and exposure programmes rather than a single fixed target-and-beam configuration.
physics_targets: Neutrino and antineutrino interactions on nucleons and nuclei
Hadron production, charm and nucleon structure
Rare processes and short-baseline oscillation searches
detection_principle: Charged particles created bubble trails in a superheated liquid inside a superconducting magnet. Photographs reconstructed tracks and secondary decays; external muon identification and selected ancillary detectors enhanced neutrino-event classification.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: Historical apparatus and published data are documented by the cited experiment publications.

timeline.event: Early particle tracks recorded and commissioning described
Neutrino, antineutrino and hadron exposure programmes

results.summary: Produced detailed exclusive interaction samples and nucleon-level measurements; results must be associated with their particular BEBC collaboration, fill and exposure.

science_scope: The record describes the named experiment as one programme; detector subsystems and repeated analyses are not counted as independent experiments.
